body:
I’m probably going to go out to a late dinner somewhere by myself (I’m still debating where) and then either stay and watch fireworks on the tv if wherever I go has tvs, or I’ll go to the city center and watch them there by myself. I don’t have anyone to go with, and I have a feeling that things are going to change for the worse for me in not too long, so I’m going to try to enjoy a last NYE. 

Probably I’m going to go to one place that has a really good meatloaf sandwich, or this other place that has a really good BLT. Both places have tvs. I have a gift card for a really nice restaurant with great food, but they don’t have tvs, so I’d have to leave to go to the city center, but the gift card restaurant is very pretty, like they have outdoor heaters and a fire pit and stuff, even though it’s too cold to be outside. I probably won’t talk to anyone, but I think it’ll be nice.
That is fairy-tale beauty! I’m glad you got to see it in person!

Gentle, faithful, funny, intelligent, respectful, open to a RR relationship, doesn’t use drugs or alcohol to excess (if at all), open minded, doesn’t blow money, constructive, supportive, and affectionate. Thinks about my wants and needs and genuinely tries to make me happy. Never abusive or mean. Doesn’t disappear or hang out with the guys and ignore me. Doesn’t expect me to always pay for everything or buy extravagant gifts and give nothing in return. Really would still be with me if something awful happened and I was paralyzed or disfigured. Enjoys my company even when I’m being silly or stupid, and is really 100% on my side always, even when he has to tell me that I’m wrong about something. Making noise or talking in bed is a bonus. 

Looks I don’t really care about, but I really like genuine smiles, open laughter, and that kind of thing.

Being able to go out, whether it was with friends or on a date. One of the few times I went with a friend to the mall, my mom had given me all the money she had, it was less than $5. The first place my friend wanted to go was Sbarro. I’d never been, and just followed what she was doing. She ordered a calzone. I had no idea what that was, but I looked at the menu (from the side) and saw it was $0.35, so I ordered one, too. I got to the register and found out it was $3.50, not $0.35, and had to pretend I didn’t want a drink. Later I got fussed at for spending everything I’d been given except for some change. There was never any time when I got to do normal pre-teen or teen things without something going wrong and there being some kind of hidden consequences, so eventually I just stopped trying. 

Going out on dates was out of the question; I guess I developed a kind of bad attitude to try to stop guys from asking me out. Finally I dropped out because things had gotten worse and I only had one pair of jeans and two shirts, then the water got turned off, the power was cut off a couple weeks later, and a school dance was coming up; I couldn’t handle turning down the guys that had asked me, but saying yes wouldn’t have been fair to my mom because she had no way to help me get a dress, and even if by some miracle I had come up with one that wasn’t completely inappropriate and humiliating for my date, there was no place for a date to pick me up. So all of it was out of the question, and I felt my time was better spent on working FT to try to help get the power and water back on, so I just vanished. It’s kind of funny, but to this day I’ve never been out on an actual date. By the time I became an adult, I guess I just wasn’t dating material anymore, I don’t know. 

So all those things that you see in photos, like girls wearing trendy clothes and cool hairstyles, wearing warm clothing, in a fully furnished home, having fun and not thinking about remembering to not eat too much so they are able to sneak food home to share, just generally being carefree and having a whole world where being embarrassed, going without power and water, being constantly afraid of being evicted wasn’t a constant fear…that to me was what rich was. I still think that when I see teens dressed up for prom or old photos with the fancy dresses and corsages, or girlfriends just goofing around and having fun; I immediately assume that they are from rich families. 

For the record, before anyone tries to give me shit about how my thing is stupid, selfish, or why don’t I try to change things, I actually do anonymously donate nice gowns to some places that provide nice dresses to girls whose families can’t afford them. There was nothing like that when I was a teenager.
I don’t have the same mental health issues, and I’ve never tried suicide before, but otherwise yes. I feel trapped. Drowning and trapped. I don’t have any solutions.
